To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the expression of the progesterone receptor is associated with the risk of recurrence in Luminal B breast cancers, and that the risk of recurrence is higher among patients who have lost progesterone receptor expression compared to those with high expression.

the expression of the progesterone receptor (PR) is associated with better outcome in breast cancer patients, and the PR loss identifies Luminal breast cancer subgroups with higher risk of relapsed disease.
the loss of progesterone receptor expression identifies a subgroup of Luminal B breast cancers that have a worse clinical outcome, and that this subgroup has a distinct gene expression profile.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the molecular determinants of the clinical heterogeneity of Luminal B breast cancers and their potential use as biomarkers of response to endocrine therapy.
the study of the molecular basis of the biological effects of progesterone in breast cancer cells, with particular emphasis on the mechanisms involved in the control of cell cycle progression.
the development of new methods of analysis for the study of complex data sets, in particular, data sets which contain a large number of variables, such as those arising in gene expression studies.
